page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The system includes 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 9 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities across memory and compute-bound tasks. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2152.0 and a multi-core score of 19030.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 65056.32. Memory performance is notable, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 4111.32 GB/sec and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 222.1 GB/sec. It demonstrates top-tier efficiency in image processing and text generation for small language models, processing 353.0 tokens per second on a 135M model.

The c7i-flex.12xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for workloads requiring high clock speeds and advanced vector extensions, such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training. Qualitatively, the flex-class hardware provides a cost-efficient option for high-density compute tasks that do not require full continuous utilization of standard compute-optimized instances. It is highly suitable for software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference.
